questions.question: A 1970s teletype terminal encodes the letter 'A' as 65 and 'a' as 97, storing each English character in a single 7-bit code. Which character-encoding standard does it use?
alternatives: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
questions.explanation: The 7-bit-per-character scheme and the classic code points (A=65, a=97) are the signature of ASCII.

questions.question: A storage array stripes data with parity so the server keeps running even after one drive fails. Which acronym names this family of multi-disk layouts?
questions.explanation: Striping, mirroring, and parity across multiple disks are the RAID family; surviving a drive failure is its defining purpose.

questions.question: A retro workstation chains a scanner and two drives on one parallel bus, each device assigned a unique ID and the last device fitted with a terminator. Which four-letter bus acronym is this?
questions.explanation: Unique device IDs on a parallel bus plus mandatory termination are the classic hallmarks of SCSI.

questions.question: On power-up a PC emits repeating beeps and halts before loading any OS when its RAM is bad, but emits one short beep and continues when all hardware passes. Which four-letter firmware routine generates these beep codes?
questions.explanation: Beep codes issued before the OS loads come from the BIOS/UEFI Power-On Self-Test hardware check.

questions.question: A PC keeps forgetting its date, time, and boot settings on every cold boot after its coin-cell battery dies, though it runs normally once configured. The battery-backed settings memory is conventionally named by which acronym?
questions.explanation: Firmware settings were traditionally held in low-power CMOS RAM kept alive by the coin-cell battery.

questions.question: When a user closes the lid, the OS tells the firmware to enter the S3 sleep state, keeping RAM powered while everything else shuts down. Which acronym names the standard that defines these power states?
questions.explanation: ACPI defines the G/S/D power states and hands device power control to the operating system.

questions.question: An email must carry a PDF attachment, yet SMTP transports only plain ASCII text, so the binary file is base64-encoded and labeled with a content type. Which standard's acronym makes such attachments possible?
questions.explanation: MIME extends email beyond plain text with content types and encodings like base64 for binary attachments.

questions.question: A company centralizes accounts so email, VPN, and intranet apps all authenticate against one hierarchical directory of users. Which four-letter protocol acronym do the clients use to query that directory?
questions.explanation: LDAP is the standard protocol for querying directory services such as Active Directory and OpenLDAP.

questions.question: A web designer must export a logo with a transparent background and sharp edges with zero compression loss, ruling out lossy JPEG. Which three-letter image format acronym applies?
questions.explanation: PNG is lossless and supports alpha transparency, making it the right choice over lossy JPEG.

questions.question: A photographer needs small photo files where smooth gradients compress well even at the cost of slight quality loss. Which format, named after the standards group that created it, fits?
questions.explanation: JPEG is lossy compression designed for continuous-tone photographs and is named for its defining committee.

questions.question: A forum avatar must be a tiny looping animation limited to a 256-color palette that plays in every browser without plugins. Which three-letter format does the designer export?
questions.explanation: GIF's 256-color palette and frame animation make it the classic format for small looping clips.

questions.question: A signup form blocks registration bots by showing distorted text that humans can read but OCR software cannot — a test 'to tell computers and humans apart.' Name the acronym.
alternatives: Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart
questions.explanation: A challenge-response that separates humans from bots is a CAPTCHA.

questions.question: A word processor displays fonts, margins, and images on screen exactly as the page will print, with no markup codes visible. Which acronym describes such editors?
alternatives: What You See Is What You Get
questions.explanation: WYSIWYG editors render the document on screen exactly as it will appear in final output.

questions.question: In the 1990s an office carried voice calls plus 128 kbps data over ordinary telephone lines before broadband arrived. Which four-letter acronym names this digital telephony service?
questions.explanation: ISDN delivered digital voice and low-rate data over existing phone lines, typified by 128 kbps bonded channels.

questions.question: Twenty office PCs with private 192.168.x.x addresses share one public IP while the router rewrites each outbound packet's source and tracks the sessions. Which three-letter acronym names this technique?
questions.explanation: NAT lets many private hosts share public addresses by translating source IP/port at the router.

questions.question: A technician must open an encrypted remote command-line session to a Linux server over an untrusted network. Which three-letter protocol acronym should they use?
questions.explanation: SSH encrypts remote terminal sessions and authentication, replacing insecure Telnet.

questions.question: A poster must include a square barcode that any phone camera can scan to open a website. Which two-letter acronym names this matrix code?
questions.explanation: QR (Quick Response) codes store URLs in a 2D pattern readable from any orientation.

questions.question: A developer receives app settings as human-readable text built from key-value pairs inside curly braces, a format derived from JavaScript. Name its acronym.
questions.explanation: JSON is the dominant lightweight data-interchange format for APIs and configuration files.

questions.question: A user wants mail to stay on the server and stay synchronized between their phone and laptop instead of downloading to one device. Which four-letter protocol acronym should the mail client use?
questions.explanation: IMAP keeps messages on the server and syncs state across devices, unlike POP3 which downloads to a single client.

questions.question: A new laptop plugs into the office network and instantly receives an IP address, subnet mask, gateway, and DNS server with no manual setup. Which four-letter protocol acronym provided them?
questions.explanation: DHCP automatically leases IP configuration to devices when they join a network.
